newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates steady, seen softening next week.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates steady, seen softening next week.

text.p: Indian call money money was trading at 10.75-11.25 percent in late morning trade on Wednesday, compared to the opening level of 10.25-11.00 percent, dealers said. The rates will move in a narrow range, they said.
Call rates have been steady at 10.75-11.0 percent this week.
"There is not much of movement," said a manager at a state-run bank in Bombay. "Deals are not of the same magnitude as before as lendable surpluses are dwindling fast," he said.
The fall in lendable resources are partly due to increased credit offtake, he said.

A proposed cut in cash reserve requirements of banks by 50 basis points to 10.5 percent on January 4, announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) last week, is expected to boost liquidity and ease call rates next week.
"Call rates won't fall to 2.0-3.0 percent but should see 7.0-8.0 percent level next week," said a treasury manager.
